notes:
Account brief: DevQuarry builds an IDE-embedded copilot focused on inline code completion and low-latency streaming for enterprise customers. Heavy emphasis on reproducibility and version pinning to ensure consistent completions across releases.

Key requests / product signals:
- Must be able to pin model binary + tokenizer pair per workspace (per-customer pin). deterministic seeding for completions to reproduce prior suggestions.
- Canary + rollout support: want automatic canary to 5% of users, eval gates on code-quality regressions (unit test pass rates, lint scores, F1-like token overlap metrics).
- Low-latency streaming: 50ms first-token target for local devs (close-proximity infra), 100ms 95p for remote.
- Model fallbacks: prefer policy-based routing by latency then cost; when pinned model unavailable, fall back to a compatible quantized variant. Need configurable TTL for fallback.
- Audit + provenance: every completion must include model_version id + commit hash in telemetry; retention controls for snippets.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2025-11-12: Intro call (AE Maya) — high-level product fit, they described reproducibility painpoint: 'our support queues blow up after model upgrades'.
- 2025-12-01: Security questionnaire sent; they asked for SOC2 evidence and KMS integration notes. (drive link: /drive/security/devquarry-security-questions.docx)
- 2026-01-15: Deep technical sync with SE Diego — discussed kernel selection, quantized model variants, and determinism strategies. SE agreed to prototype pinned-model + deterministic-seed sample.
- 2026-02-08: POC kickoff: 30-day internal POC to validate canary mechanics and eval gates. Scope: 10 dev seats, two model versions (v1.2 and v1.3-beta).
- 2026-02-18: Fireflies transcript FF-99823 — customer emphasized need for 'exactly reproducible completions for bug-ticket replays'.
- 2026-02-24: POC baseline results — initial latency OK, but stochastic completions observed when caching enabled; investigating KV cache warm/cold determinism. Jira ticket INF-3221 opened.

POC metrics they care about:
- Determinism rate (identical completion on repeat with same seed/context) target > 99%
- First-token latency 95p < 100ms
- Regression score on curated eval set (code-safety + unit-test pass) no worse than current production baseline
- Cost per 1k tokens target within 1.4x current incumbent

Quotes / snippets from stakeholders:
- 'If we can't pin a version and prove repeatability, we can't offer reproducible developer sessions' — Lead Eng (Anya Petrova)
- 'Canaries must be able to automatically rollback on eval gate failure' — CTO (Ramon Delgado)

Open decisions / blockers:
- Legal needs to approve data residency SLA (they want EU-only for some customers) — slows private deployment signoff.
- Deterministic caching approach: runtime change vs client-side seed enforcement. SE recommended trying runtime-level deterministic KV cache first.
- Pricing for Dedicated pool (they will likely want reserved capacity once canary passes). Pricing deck in drive: /drive/pricing/devquarry-redwood-pricing-v2.pdf
